questions.q: How does sharding differ in scope from the table partitioning covered in Lesson 15?
options: Partitioning splits one table inside one database; sharding splits one logical dataset across multiple separate physical databases
They are exactly the same thing with different names
Sharding only applies to indexes, while partitioning only applies to tables
Partitioning works across multiple databases, while sharding works inside one database
questions.explain: Partitioning stays inside a single database's storage; sharding is a distribution pattern across many independent databases, each with its own compute and storage.

questions.q: What does Azure's shard map manager do?
options: Tracks which range of a sharding key lives on which shard, and routes queries to the correct shard automatically
Automatically merges all shards into a single database
Encrypts data differently on each shard
Compresses data on every shard using PAGE compression
questions.explain: The shard map manager is the lookup database that lets the client library route each query to the correct physical shard based on the sharding key.

questions.q: What does the split-merge service do in Azure's Elastic Database tools?
options: Physically moves ranges of data between shards to rebalance them as shards grow unevenly
Automatically writes cross-shard T-SQL joins for you
Deletes shards that are underused
Converts a sharded database back into a single Managed Instance
questions.explain: Split-merge splits an oversized range in two or merges small ranges together, moving data between shards without an application outage.

questions.q: Why are cross-shard queries a real complexity cost of sharding?
options: A query needing data from multiple shards can't be a single T-SQL statement — it must fan out to each shard and combine results
Cross-shard queries are automatically optimized with zero extra complexity
Sharding makes all queries faster with no downsides
Cross-shard queries are not possible under any circumstances
questions.explain: Unlike a single database, a sharded architecture requires fanning a query out across databases and combining the results, typically in application code or with elastic query.

questions.q: Per this lesson, when should a DBA actually reach for sharding?
options: Only when a single database's measured ceiling — size, compute, or throughput — is the real, confirmed constraint, not a guess about future scale
On every new project, by default, regardless of size
Whenever more than two tables exist in the database
Instead of table partitioning, in every case
questions.explain: Sharding brings real complexity costs (cross-shard queries, manual rebalancing, no cross-shard referential integrity), so it should only be adopted once a single database's actual measured ceiling is the confirmed constraint.
